title: memory-pressure-backpressure-arch-deepdive-notes
summary: Notes and decisions from an architecture deep-dive on GPU memory-pressure containment and request-level backpressure. Goal: design a pragmatic, incremental solution that prevents high-memory requests from causing tail-latency spikes while preserving throughput for latency-sensitive traffic.
agenda: Review recent tail-latency incidents under bursty small+large mixes
Telemetry gaps: what metrics we need from GPUs and runtime
Design proposals: soft/hard memory ceilings, per-request costing, eviction and compaction
Fallback strategies: model variant routing and quantized spill-to-CPU
discussion_notes:
Background: Over the last 3 weeks we've seen two incidents where a mix of short, low-token chat requests and a small number of long-document summarization calls pushed GPU memory usage above safe thresholds. This caused the runtime to stall while collecting memory and IO, producing ~300–400ms p99 spikes for latency-sensitive routes.

Telemetry gaps: Mei called out missing signals: per-device soft-resident-bytes (inc. pinned KV), per-request peak-resident estimate, cross-GPU aggregate pending-eviction count, and precise KV cache fragmentation metrics. We agreed to add a small telemetry shim to expose 'estimated-request-memory' from the planner + 'kv-frag-score' from the KV store.

Design proposals discussed:
1) Soft vs hard ceilings: Soft ceiling triggers admission control (queuing or gentle backpressure) when device resident > soft_limit (e.g., 80% of rated mem). Hard ceiling rejects or immediately routes to fallback when > hard_limit (e.g., 95%). Soft_limit should be configurable per-queue/model.

2) Per-request costing: Planner should emit an estimated memory cost (based on seq length, kv cache delta, and model variant) used by the scheduler to decide immediate acceptance or queue. For types we can't estimate, use conservative upper bound and mark request as 'probe' to allow runtime to learn cost distribution.

3) Eviction policy: Replace naive LRU eviction with a prioritized eviction that preserves low-latency conversational KV entries (pinned) and evicts long-tail cold snapshots first. Introduce TTL bands and conversation-priority flags from convo metadata.

4) KV compaction / compression: Prototype a transient compaction pass that converts float16 KV blocks to a compact packed representation when under memory pressure and that supports fast unpack on demand. Also discussed aggressive delta-merge for repeated prefixes to reduce duplicate KV entries across conversations.

5) Fallback routing: If the request cannot be admitted within a target enqueue window (default 50ms for low-latency lanes), automatically fallback to one of: a) smaller quantized model variant (same API), b) CPU-based inference with lower throughput, or c) deferred acceptance with client-visible Retry-After header. Routing policy should be policy-driven per-route.

6) Priority lanes: Introduce two admission lanes: "fast" (strict target latency, limited concurrency) and "bulk" (higher token throughput, tolerant latency). The scheduler should reserve headroom on each GPU for a minimal number of fast lanes to prevent starvation.

Operational considerations: Jon emphasized SRE-runbook changes for graceful rejection vs timeouts and alerts on repeated hard-limit rejections. Diego wants to avoid global stop-the-world eviction — prefer localized per-device containment.

Prototype plan: implement telemetry shim (Mei), planner estimate integration (Priya + Hannah), experimental soft limiter + per-request queue (Liam + Diego). KV compaction prototype to run behind feature flag (Hannah + Diego).
decisions: Add per-device soft_limit (default 80%) and hard_limit (default 95%) in runtime config
Planner MUST produce a conservative 'estimated_request_memory' field on every request; runtime will use it for admission decisions
Eviction policy will be priority-aware: pinned conversation KV > short-recent KV > cold snapshots
Implement two admission lanes (fast, bulk) with headroom reservation per GPU
Fallback order: quantized-variant -> CPU fallback -> Retry-After deferred acceptance
KV compaction will be prototyped as an opt-in feature-flagged path; production gating after perf benchmarks

risks: Estimations may be overly conservative and throttle throughput — need to iterate with real traces
Compaction unpack latency could negate gains for fast requests if not carefully optimized
Fallbacks may degrade user experience for heavy workloads unless route-level policies are clear
Headroom reservation lowers peak utilization; product tradeoff between latency SLO and cost must be documented
